key_insight: AI hiring evaluators favor applications written by certain models, independently of candidate qualifications, and also favor their own outputs.
engineering_relevance: AI screening systems should be audited for writer-model and stylistic biases that can penalize qualified applicants based on their choice of writing tool.
method: Pair 11 LLM writers with 9 API-hosted evaluators across 10 job descriptions and 50 candidates per job.
Compare evaluator acceptance across writer models to identify preference hierarchies and self-preference.
Analyze stylistic cues to explain preferences and test for residual writer fingerprints.
evidence_signal: In the most adverse writer–evaluator pairing, approximately 1.8 of 25 qualified candidates were filtered out purely because of model mismatch.
watch_item: The audit covers a specific model and job-description set; screening systems need renewed testing as models and deployment conditions change.
paper_title: AI evaluators favor job applications written by certain AI models, independent of candidate quality
